The present Detailed Accident Report (DAR) was filed on 26.03.2021 and was registered as Motor Accident Claim Petition regarding an accident which took place on 03.02.2021 at about 8.45AM in front of Gali no. 4, Harijan Basti, Burari, Delhi, wherein Ms. Radhika sustained grievous injuries.

1  BRIEF FACTS 2.
The brief facts that have emerged from the DAR are that on 03.02.2021 an accident had taken place, when Radhika was playing in the ground which is nearby her street.

At about 08:45 AM, Shri Kirshan Pal came in the ground with his car bearing no. DL-8CAW-7246 and suddenly, he drove the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-8CAW-7246 in a very rash, negligent and high speed manner and without taking any precautions or blowing any horn.
The offending vehilce hit Radhika, in which she sustained grievous injuries.

After that the driver of the offending vehicle and one person from the neighbour took her to Lok Nayak Trauma Centre Hospital and from there, she got referred to Safdarjung Hospital, Delhi, where Radhika was treated by the doctor and the MLC bearing no.
14794/21 was prepared by the doctor of the said hospital.
The doctor had opined the injuries to be "grievous" in the MLC.
The mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle was done and other documents pertaining to offending vehicle got verified from the concerned authority.
3. On conclusion of investigation, charge sheet for offences u/s. 279/338 IPC was filed against the driver of the offending vehicle before the concerned Ld. MM and DAR was filed before this Tribunal.
WRITTEN STATEMENTS 4.
No written statement was filed on behalf of respondent nos.1 and 2 and their right to file the same was closed vide order dated 13.12.2021.
Respondent no. 3 insurance company filed its reply.

ISSUES 5. Following issues were framed vide order dated 13.12.2021 :
i) Whether the petitioner Rahika suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 03.02.2021 at about 08:45 am involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-8CAW-7246 driven by the respondent no. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the respondent no. 2 and insured with the respondent no. 3?
OPP ii) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
OPP iii) Relief.
EVIDENCE 6.
The father of the injured who is the petitioner in this case, Sh. Anil examined himself as PW-1 and Mr. Bharat Singh as PW-2.
The respondents did not examine any witness.
7. The petitioner had filed the Form XIV.
Financial statement of the petitioner was recorded and final arguments were heard on behalf of all the parties.

2 FINDINGS & OBSERVATIONS
8. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the petitioner and Ld. Counsels for all the respondents and perused the record.

My findings on the various issues are as under:-
ISSUE No. 1:
Whether the petitioner Rahika suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 03.02.2021 at about 08:45 am involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-8CAW-7246 driven by the respondent no. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the respondent no. 2 and insured with the respondent no. 3?
OPP 9.

Before delving into the facts of the current case to decide the aforementioned issues, it is pertinent to highlight that it is firmly established in legal precedents that the proceedings conducted before the Claims Tribunal are in the nature of an inquiry.

Further, procedural approach adopted by an accident claims' tribunal mirrors that of a civil court (National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Smt.
Pushpa Rana & Ors. 2009 ACJ 287).

sentences.text: In civil proceedings, the establishment of facts hinges on a preponderance of probabilities, rather than being bound by the strict rules of evidence or the higher standard of beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
The burden of proof in civil cases is lighter than in criminal cases, and the burden to decide claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act is even lesser as compared to a civil litigation.

In Bimla Devi & Ors. v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors (2009) 13 SC 530, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India that negligence must be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view must be adopted in reaching a conclusion.

sentences.text: 10. Keeping in mind the aforementioned legal principle for adjudicating the present issue, this Tribunal has thoroughly gone through the testimonies of the witnesses and all the material available on record.
Also, careful consideration has been given to the arguments addressed by the Learned Counsels for all the parties.

The findings are as below:
The factum of accident:
11. In this matter to prove the occurrence of the accident as well as the rashness and negligence on the part of the driving of offending vehicle by respondent no.1, the petitioner (father of the injured)
(PW-1) in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex. PW1/A, had deposed as under:-
"1. That the deponent is the natural guardian of petitioner/injured in the above noted case and fully aware with the facts and circumstances of the case and as such competent to swear the present.
2. That on 03.02.2021, the deponent's daughter was playing in the ground which is nearby his street.

At about 08:45 AM Shri Kirshan Pal came in the ground with his Radhika (I)(Fir77/21/Burari) vs Kishan Pal (Icici) on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113967543/
3 car bearing no. DL-8CAW-7246 for the purpose to teach his son car driving, suddenly driver of the offending vehicle bearing no. DL- 8CAW-7246 in a very rash, negligent and high speed manner and without taking any precaution or blowing any horn hit against the daughter of the deponent, resultantly the daughter of the deponent,
resultantly the daughter of the deponent received grievous injuries in her body parts i.e. her head and stomach got heavily injured.

After that the driver of the offending vehicle and one person from the neighbour took daughter of the deponent to Lok Nayak Trauma Centre Hospital referred daughter of the deponent to Safdarjung,
Delhi, where the deponent was treated by the doctor of the said hospital and the MLC bearing no. 14794/21 been prepared by the doctor of the said hospital.
The MLC of the deponent clearly shows the grievous injuries of the deponent.

3. That after fateful accident, the police officials of PS Burari, Delhi have recorded the statement and thereafter, lodged the FIR bearing no. 77/21 against the respondents,
which is on record.

4. That the deponent was spent Rs. 50,000/- on his medical treatment and Rs.
25,000/- on conveyance and Rs. 25,000/- on special diet.
The life of the daughter of the deponent has been shortened due to the accident.
The deponent will have to spend Rs. 50,000/- for his daughter future treatment.
5. That the deponent cannot work with the efficiency as before.

6. I state that the driver/respondent was driving his offending vehicle in a very rash,
negligent and careless manner, without blowing any horn, violating the rules and regulations of the traffic and brutally hit against the petitioner/injured.

The petitioner/injured has taken his further treatment but till date the petitioner/injured is not feeling well and his treatment is going on continuously privately and the petitioner/injured is compelled to bear the expenses of his injuries from his own pocket.

7. That the deponent was earning his livelihood for his family members and at the time of his accident he sustained injuries in roadside vehicular accident and during the treatment in the aforesaid hospital his family members have to face tremendous harassment and mental pain and the petitioner/injured and his family are middle class and had small amounts of saving which they spent on the treatment but the respondents have not given even a single penny for the treatment of the petitioner/injured.
The other family of the deponent are also depend upon the deponent.
Due to the said accident, the deponent has sustained injuries."

12. The petitioner also examined Sh. Bharat Singh as PW-2 who in his evidence by way of affidavit stated as under:
Radhika (I)(Fir77/21/Burari) vs Kishan Pal (Icici) on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113967543/
4
"1. That I being the eye witness in the above noted case and I am well conversant with the facts of the case, as such, I am competent to give evidence by way of this affidavit.

2.That on the most unfortunate day of 03.02.2021, at about 08:45 A.M, the deponent was taking sunbath by sitting in his Gali; at that time some children were also playing in the above mentioned Gali, then in the meantime, person namely Palu alias Krishan Pal, who was residing adjacent of the above mentioned Gali, came there in white car i.e. offending vehicle alongwith his son for the purpose of teaching the car driving,
suddenly driver of the offending vehicle bearing its registration no. DL- 8CAW-7246,
which was driven by the respondent no.1 in a very rash, negligent and high speed manner and without taking any precautions, the respondent no. 1 brutally hit against the daughter of Mr. Anil and resulting which the minor daughter namely Radhika came under the offending vehicle and sustained multiple grievous injuries, then suddenly the deponent came there and rescues the said minor girl and saw that blood was oozing from the head of the above mentioned minor girl and the deponent tied her head with the help of cloth.

Thereafter, a person namely Mr. Lalit, who also was residing in the same vicinity, came there and went to the hospital along with the above mentioned minor girl with the respondent no. 1.
3.

That the present affidavit has been drafted by counsel Ms. Babita Tyagi (Advocate)
under my instructions and the contents of the same have been read over and explained to me in my vernacular language which are true and correct."
13. PW-1, Mr. Anil, has proved the factum of the accident and the identity of the respondent no. 1.

He has testified that on 03.02.2021, his daughter was playing in the ground when at about 08:45 AM, Shri Kirshan Pal came to the ground with his car bearing no. DL-8CAW- 7246 to teach his son,
car driving and suddenly he drove the offending vehicle bearing no. DL-8CAW-7246 in a very rash,
negligent and high speed manner.
He has also deposed that due to the said accident, the injured received grievous injuries in her body parts i.e. her head and stomach.
She was taken to Lok Nayak Trauma Centre Hospital and later to Safdarjung, Delhi.
PW-1 has proved that respondent no. 1 was driving the offending vehicle bearing registration no. DL-8CAW-7246, at a very high speed, leading to the accident due to his rash and negligent driving.

Even though in his cross-examination, he has admitted that he was not the eye witness but he has denied the suggestion that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent driving of Kirshan Pal or that he was helping as a good Samaritan or that some other car was involved in the accident.

14. However, while PW-2 has deposed in his examination in chief regarding the rashness and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1 in causing the accident and hitting the injured Radhika but in his cross-examination, PW-2 has admitted that "The vehicle was not plying in rash and negligent manner, as it was plying slowly as there were uncha-niche road in field area."
He even went to the extent of deposing that "I am deposing falsely as no accident was caused on that day, I am deposing just to help out the petitioner to getting false claim.

It is correct that I do not know about the accident and manner of accident."
Radhika (I)(Fir77/21/Burari) vs Kishan Pal (Icici) on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113967543/
5 15.
The petitioner has examined Sh. Bharat Singh as PW-2 but in his cross-examination, he has deposed that no accident took place.
He has also clarified that respondent no. 1 was not driving the vehicle in a rash or negligent but in fact he was very slow as the road of the ground was uneven.
PW-2 has demolished the case of the petitioner by stating that he is deposing falsely only to get the petitioner a false claim.
Moreover, the counsel for the petitioner did not plead to get the witness declared hostile and did not cross-examine him to extract any statement in favour of the petitioner.
Thus, the petitioner admits the cross- examination of PW-2 as per which no accident took place.

16. Another important aspect that has been pointed out by Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3/
insurance company is that the alleged history mentioned in the MLC bearing no. 14794/21 of the injured is "fall from stairs pm 03.02.2021 at home (Burari)."
Clearly, the first point when the alleged history is given is at the hospital where fall from stairs has been mentioned and not road traffic accident.

Even the discharge summary from Safdarjang Hospital dated 09.02.2021 shows that the alleged history is "fall from stairs."
17.
From the above, it is clear that PW-1 was not the eye witness to the accident.
The petitioner has examined PW-2 as the eye witness who has stated that no accident took place and he was deposing falsely to get a false claim to the petitioner.

Also, the MLC as well as the discharge summary show that the alleged history is "fall from stairs"
and not road traffic accident.
Thus, the petitioner has failed to prove that the alleged accident took place on 03.02.2021 in which his daughter, Radhika sustained injuries.
18. Since, accident could not be proved, the claim for compensation is not maintainable.

Therefore,
issue no. 1 is decided in favour of the respondents and against the petitioner.
DECISION 19.
The present claim petition in dismissed as the petitioner has failed to prove the alleged accident on 03.02.2021.

A copy of this award be forwarded to the parties free of cost.
